investigation: MuseScore-named installer: shipped artifact inspection and separately labeled upstream editor source trace

questions.question: What is the supplied file?
questions.answer: A signed x64 native MuseHub installer, not the MuseScore Studio editor executable.

questions.question: What is packaged inside?
questions.answer: ZIP_MUSEHUB at offset 950496, length 35798508. The archive lists 108 entries including directories and 135511537 uncompressed bytes. It includes MuseHub.exe, updater, uninstaller, authorization service, ServiceCore.dll, WinUI/Windows App SDK libraries, fonts, and localization. No separately named MuseScore editor executable is listed.

questions.question: How does installation and launch work?
questions.answer: The manifest declares requireAdministrator. Static messages describe staging/extracting and verifying MuseHub, moving the old current directory aside, registering application/protocol/startup/uninstall entries, installing authorization and updater services, and launching MuseHub. The installer has a MuseScore-specific store-page URI. Branch execution and ordering are inferred from strings, not observed runtime or decompiled control flow.

questions.question: How does MIDI become notation?
questions.answer: The MIDI module registers mid/midi/kar readers. NotationMidiReader::read calls importMidi. The import pipeline parses MIDI, groups tracks/channels, adjusts beats, splits left/right hands and drum voices, quantizes timing, simplifies durations, separates voices, creates parts/staves and measures, adds notes/rests/keys/clefs/time signatures, ties, lyrics, tempo and chord names.
questions.limitation: This is verified against the pinned public source commit; that source is not contained in the supplied installer and binary equivalence was not established.

questions.question: How does the score become sheet music?
questions.answer: The PDF writer prepares a Qt QPdfWriter and asks the notation painting layer to paint the score into PDF pages. It supports per-part and multi-part output. The MusicXML module independently registers XML/MusicXML/MXL readers and writers.

questions.question: Does this establish full-song audio-to-score transcription?
questions.answer: No audio-to-note transcription engine was established from the supplied installer. The editor audio module inspected registers WAV/MP3/OGG/FLAC/AAC writers, while MIDI and MusicXML have explicit readers. For the original workflow, an external transcription stage supplies MIDI/MusicXML to the notation editor.
questions.limitation: This is not an exhaustive audit of all MuseScore source, plugins or optional external products.

evidence.conclusion: Native PE32+ x86_64; no CLI directory, managed metadata or CIL available.
Complete supported PE resource tree inventory: 11 resources.
Root PE identity; nested PE resource archives not traversed automatically.

evidence.kind: Ordinary Python static strings, not REA Evidence
evidence.conclusion: File offsets and encodings retained; strings establish references and messages, not executed branches.
Resource slices verified against REA payload SHA-256.

evidence.kind: Ordinary Python extraction / integrity verification, not REA Evidence
evidence.conclusion: Six selected files decoded from ZIP compression method 95 (XZ); all CRC32 values verified; all five non-manifest files match the package manifest SHA-256.
Six public MuseScore source files preserved with commit/blob identities and original URLs.

limitations: No installer, bundled executable, service or editor was executed.
No function-level native decompiler provider was configured; native call order, branches, registry writes and networking were not dynamically verified.
REA and Python zipfile did not support ZIP compression method 95. A format-aware stdlib XZ decoder materialized selected members and verified CRC32 plus the package manifest SHA-256.
Only the selected six archive members were materialized; the complete 108-entry member index was retained.
Common installed MuseScore paths and uninstall entries were checked without finding an editor executable. This was not an exhaustive whole-disk search.
Studio source findings are separate from the supplied MuseHub binary and do not establish the editor release that MuseHub would download.
Persistent MCP registration was missing. The CLI supplied static analysis without editing Codex configuration or installing a native decompiler.
